newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, shrugs off economic data.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, shrugs off economic data.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday, shrugging off trade data made available, dealers said.
They said the market remained driven by liquidity.
"Trading was like a yo-yo in the afternoon based on liquidity anticipation. People keep asking about liquidity but only a few talked about data," one U.S. bank dealer said.

He said the trade surplus data made available on Tuesday was within expectations and led to only a minor reaction on the market. Spot rupiah was at 2,393.10/93.50 at 0915 GMT, compared with an intra-day high of 2,392.0. It opened at 2,395.0/96.0.

Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,391.60/92.25 and 2,394.60/95.10, respectively. Dealers said the rupiah strengthened sharply against the dollar at midday on worries over the liquidity outlook, driving swap rates up.
But they said the worries were reversed late in the afternoon as swaps eased off highs, offering a good chance for operators to speculate on differing interpretations.
Overnight swaps were at 0.15/0.25. Tom/next swaps edged down to 0.2/0.3 from 0.35 in the afternoon after opening at 0.20/0.25 points. One-week was back to 1.7 after 2.2/2.4.
Dealers said offshore players were forced into stop-loss dollar selling in mid-afternoon on liquidity worries.
They said swaps cooled off after rising at midday as some operators moved to cash out from the spot market.
One-month swaps edged down to 10.50/11.50 from 12.00/12.75, two to 23.0/24.0 from 24.0/26.0, three to 35.00/36.25 from 35.5/37.0 and six to 75.0/76.5 from 75.5/76.5.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,384/2,576 and the conversion band to 2,384/2,432 on Tuesday after lowering the rupiah by one point on Monday.
